description: §55.1 / §63.5 — the soft-deprecated validator spelling `<nick is some length(>=3)>`. It declares the cell (before S462 impl#1 silently dropped it) and is the same predicate as `<nick is given>`: typing "ab" leaves a present value, so the presence predicate passes and does not short-circuit, and `length(>=3)` fails — errors = [.LengthFailed] only, #all renders one .scrml-error, isValid false. One W-IS-SOME-DEPRECATED (Info). Runtime identical to forms/is-given-validator.
rationale: §55.1 (S462) — `<x is some>` is the soft-deprecated spelling of `<x is given>`: the same predicate, the same `.NotSome` tag, the same short-circuit (§55.12), and each site SHALL surface W-IS-SOME-DEPRECATED. §42.2.5 — `""`-like present values pass the presence predicate (it is not `req`). Provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S462 "a, validator too, go".
